Axis: num
- Register: "R60/2000-A-NL1-21.30"
- Document: "R60/2000-A-NL1-21-30"

The register uses a dot separator "21.30" while the document uses a hyphen "21-30". This is a number/year format difference. The certificate document itself says "R60/2000-A-NL1-21-30" — looking at the document text: "Number R60/2000-A-NL1-21-30". Also the source PDF path is "r060-2000-nl1-2021-30.pdf" which uses hyphens.

The rules say: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

This clearly denotes the same certificate — same prefix R60/2000-A-NL1, same issuing year 21 (2021), same number 30, register id 5422 matches cert_id 5422. The difference is just the separator between "21" and "30": "." vs "-".

So verdict: same-entity, best_value = register's canonical form "R60/2000-A-NL1-21.30", why: it's a format difference (dot vs hyphen separator) denoting the same certificate; the register's canonical form wins per rules.

Interesting note: typically the legal instrument would be preferred, but the rule explicitly says number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate use the register's canonical form. Also the register id matches cert_id 5422, confirming same entity.
